title: Synchronous and asynchronous distance learning of anaphora in foreign languages: An experimental study
reason: Compares synchronous, asynchronous and control groups on anaphora tests. Moodle access is monitored but never analysed; the only correlations relate test scores to proficiency and self-reported motivation (MSLQ), so no LMS indicator or activity-product indicator enters an analysis.

extraction.country: Brazil (Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul)
extraction.design: experimental (2 experimental groups + control), Spearman correlations, Kruskal-Wallis
extraction.n_quote: a short course was taught in the first semester of 2020 to 45 under- graduate students with a major in English or Spanish at the Federal University of Rio Grande do
extraction.lms_indicators: Moodle access and forum/exercise participation monitored (asynchronous group) but not analysed
extraction.outcome_or_construct: anaphora reading/writing test scores; MSLQ task value and self-efficacy (self-report)
extraction.notes: Body text is English (Portuguese abstract only), so E6 does not apply. Reported Spearman correlations are pretest score ↔ proficiency/self-reported motivation (e.g. self-efficacy rho = 0.515), i.e. achievement ↔ self-report, not indicator ↔ outcome; the rho symbol is lost in the extracted text.
